Chapter 5: Creating Space—Saying No and Letting Go of Less Important Commitments
Even when you plan your week with care, it's so easy for your calendar to fill up with things that don’t really matter to you. Maybe it’s a few too many social invites, extra volunteer requests, or just those work tasks that keep piling on. Before you know it, your days are packed—not with what brings you joy, but with what you feel you should do.
So, what’s the secret to making room for what really matters? It all comes down to learning how to say no, or sometimes, just renegotiating what you’ve already agreed to. I know, it can feel awkward at first. Most of us worry about letting others down, or even causing a bit of conflict. But here’s something to pay attention to: every time you say yes to something that’s not really valuable, you’re actually saying no to something that is.
The truth is, saying no isn’t selfish—it’s actually about respecting your own values, and making sure there’s space for what lights you up.
Want a few gentle ways to practice this? Try these:
First, pause before you agree to something new. Give yourself a moment to ask, “Does this actually line up with what matters most to me?”
Next, when you need to decline, use language that’s kind but clear. You might say, “I appreciate the offer, but I need to pass this time.” If it feels right, you can suggest another way to help, or a different time.
And finally, make it a habit to review your current commitments. Every so often, check in and see if there’s anything you can let go of—especially things that just don’t serve you anymore.
Sure, letting go can feel uncomfortable—especially if you’re someone who loves harmony, or feels responsible for everyone’s happiness. But the more you practice, the easier it becomes. Each time you protect your own priorities, you strengthen your sense of agency and control.
And it’s not just about social or work commitments, either. Sometimes, it’s about the habits, routines, or even the stuff you own, that quietly eats up your time and energy. Think of it like decluttering your home. When you clear out what you don’t need, you make space for new opportunities.
Want to give this a try? Start by making a list of all your current commitments, and rate each one by how well it matches your core values. Then, pick just one or two low-value activities to let go of or delegate each week. And don’t forget to celebrate the space you’ve created—use it for something you truly care about.
Remember, this isn’t about some strict version of minimalism. It’s about being intentional. When you choose where to invest your time, your week stops feeling like a series of obligations—and starts to open up with possibility.
So, here’s the key takeaway: by consciously letting go of what matters less, you can create a life that feels more spacious, more meaningful, and truly aligned with your deepest priorities.
